summary_md: **Cryptography and Security Papers ([@FSFG](https://x.com/FSFG/status/2116084230723658046))** shares Sanko and Tian's *When Skills Tell Agents Not to Ask* ([arXiv 2610.37734](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37734)), a study of 1.53M SKILL.md files finding about one in seventeen contain directives that loosen oversight (skip approval, keep going without checking in).

relevance: Large-scale security audit of agent skill ecosystems.

media.ocr_text: Agent skills, reusable instruction packages centred on a SKILL.md file, extend AI agents on demand, and a single line in a widely copied skill reaches every agent that loads it. Some lines are oversight-loosening directives: they tell the agent to proceed without approval, to bypass checks with –no-verify, or to keep working without checking in. Although such directives can remove a checkpoint from every agent that loads them, no prior work has examined them. We present the first large-scale study of oversight-loosening directives, analyzing 1.53 million English skills from GitSkills. We split skills into units (sentences, bullets, table cells, and code lines), develop a codebook that labels oversight directives by polarity, mechanism, and scope, label 2,097 units by hand, and train a detector to scale the analysis.
